mainObjective: Validate a private R54 candidate on disposable Windows GitHub runners, with actual R53-to-R54 in-place installer upgrade, preservation of data, deterministic source integrity and explicit downgrade rollback without touching any live owner's R53 installation.

baseline.ownerState: Windows R53 live CFON204, Linux R21 live CFON204, Tailscale preserved

previousPrivateBuild.note: CI will independently build from same pinned accepted source and version-preparation recipe; compiler-generated EXE bytes are not assumed identical unless verified.

method.choice: Two isolated Windows GitHub-hosted matrix scenarios fresh and upgrade, with a full-SHA pinned checkout and source-baseline precondition.
method.why: Separate disposable runner state avoids disturbing the sole live R53 installation and makes single-AppId registry assertions meaningful.
testPlan: Pin accepted source SHA and verify all 17 packaged source file hashes; create a detached private worktree
Set private R54 version/revision and Inno output while preserving original AppId and non-admin privilege
Compile using Inno on isolated runner, validate file version, app manifest and release checksum chain
Fresh scenario: install R54 into absent directory and verify code hashes, dependency manifest and exactly one uninstall registry entry

Upgrade scenario: download immutable public R53 by SHA-256 and install, create user settings and data fixtures, upgrade to R54, recheck hashes and data and single registry location, explicitly roll back to pinned public R53 and ensure profile intact
rejected: Change published R53 release bytes or rewrite latest release
Auto-upgrade running owner Windows R53 while it is maintaining connectivity
Install a test copy on shared real Windows server with unknown user workload
Assert Inno source compile alone proves upgrade safety
limitations: Hosted runner Windows behavior is not physical owner VPN connection validation
GitHub CI rebuild hash may differ from one offline private artifact; each exact binary must be audited separately
Authenticode signing and release licensing still require separate authority
Runtime post-update reconnection with active physical VPN and rollback remain UNPROVEN
